### Welcome

This is our Geocomputation lab on Employer-Household Dynamics. This is an R analysis [inspired by this post](https://walker-data.com/posts/lodes-2020/)

### Libraries

```{r}
library(lehdr)
library(tigris)
library(mapgl)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(mapview)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
```

### Data

Our data is from the [Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics (LEHD)](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/) study from the US Census Bureau. When interacting with data like these, we should always think: "is there an r package that can make interacting with this data easier?". And the answer is yes!

The [lehdr package](https://jamgreen.github.io/lehdr/index.html) allows users to interface with the [Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics (LEHD)](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/) Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES) dataset, returned as tidy data frames

```{r}
hi_od <- grab_lodes(
  state      = "hi",
  year       = 2022,
  lodes_type = "od",
  job_type   = "JT00",
  segment    = "S000",
  state_part = "main",
  agg_geo    = "tract",
  geometry   = TRUE
) |>
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "w_geometry")
```

How did this `grab_lodes()` function work

```{r}
?grab_lodes
```

What do these column names mean?

Each row is one home-tract-to-work-tract pair. The numbers count **jobs** (in your call, `JT00` means all jobs), so a person with two jobs can appear twice.

| Column | Meaning |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `year` | Data year (2022) |
| `state` | State abbreviation |
| `w_tract` | GEOID of the **work** tract |
| `h_tract` | GEOID of the **home** tract |
| `S000` | Total jobs in this home-to-work flow |
| `SA01` | Jobs held by workers aged 29 or younger |
| `SA02` | Workers aged 30–54 |
| `SA03` | Workers aged 55 or older |
| `SE01` | Jobs earning \$1,250/month or less |
| `SE02` | \$1,251–\$3,333/month |
| `SE03` | More than \$3,333/month |
| `SI01` | Goods-producing industries (agriculture, mining, construction, manufacturing) |
| `SI02` | Trade, transportation and utilities |
| `SI03` | All other services (government, health, education, hospitality, etc.) |
| `w_geometry` / `h_geometry` | Tract polygons for the work and home ends |

### Analysis

Define destination point

```{r}
dest_point <- st_sfc(st_point(c(-157.9225, 21.3187)), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(hi_od))

# One row per work tract, keeping only the ID and its polygon
w_tracts <- hi_od[!duplicated(hi_od$w_tract), "w_tract"]

dest_geoid <- w_tracts$w_tract[lengths(st_intersects(w_tracts, dest_point)) > 0]
dest_geoid
```

Filter flows and turn into long

```{r}
top_commutes <- hi_od |>
  filter(w_tract == dest_geoid, S000 >= 25, h_tract != w_tract)

to_lonlat <- function(g) {
  g |>
    st_transform(26904) |>        # UTM 4N for accurate interior points
    st_point_on_surface() |>
    st_transform(4326) |>
    st_coordinates()
}

h_xy <- to_lonlat(top_commutes$h_geometry)
w_xy <- to_lonlat(top_commutes$w_geometry)

top_commutes <- top_commutes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>           # drops w_geometry (the active column)
  select(-h_geometry) |>          # h_geometry is a second sfc column, drop it too
  mutate(h_lon = h_xy[, 1], h_lat = h_xy[, 2],
         w_lon = w_xy[, 1], w_lat = w_xy[, 2])
```

Build curved arcs

```{r}
make_arc <- function(x1, y1, x2, y2, n = 60, curve = 0.25) {
  mx <- (x1 + x2) / 2; my <- (y1 + y2) / 2
  cx <- mx - (y2 - y1) * curve               # control point offset
  cy <- my + (x2 - x1) * curve
  t  <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
  st_linestring(cbind(
    (1 - t)^2 * x1 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cx + t^2 * x2,
    (1 - t)^2 * y1 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cy + t^2 * y2
  ))
}

flows_sf <- top_commutes |>
  mutate(
    geometry = pmap(list(h_lon, h_lat, w_lon, w_lat), make_arc),
    tooltip  = paste0(S000, " commuters<br>from tract ", h_tract)
  ) |>
  st_as_sf(crs = 4326)

origins_sf <- top_commutes |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("h_lon", "h_lat"), crs = 4326)

dest_sf <- top_commutes |>
  slice(1) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("w_lon", "w_lat"), crs = 4326)

```

Map

```{r}
max_jobs <- max(flows_sf$S000)

m <- maplibre(
  style   = carto_style("positron"),
  center  = c(-157.98, 21.42),
  zoom    = 9.6,
  pitch   = 50,
  bearing = -20
) |>
  add_line_layer(
    id         = "flows",
    source     = flows_sf,
    line_color = interpolate(
      column = "S000",
      values = c(25, max_jobs),
      stops  = c("#f06400", "#00c800")     # orange -> green, echoing the original
    ),
    line_width = interpolate(
      column = "S000",
      values = c(25, max_jobs),
      stops  = c(1, 8)
    ),
    line_opacity = 0.8,
    tooltip      = "tooltip",
    hover_options = list(line_color = "#ffff00")
  ) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id           = "origins",
    source       = origins_sf,
    circle_color = "#f06400",
    circle_radius = 3,
    circle_opacity = 0.8
  ) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id                  = "destination",
    source              = dest_sf,
    circle_color        = "#00c800",
    circle_radius       = 8,
    circle_stroke_color = "white",
    circle_stroke_width = 2
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    "Commuters to the airport / JBPHH tract",
    values = c("Fewer", "More"),
    colors = c("#f06400", "#00c800"),
    type   = "continuous"
  )

m
```

### Your Turn

Challenge 1: Recreate [this figure](https://github.com/jamgreen/lehdr/blob/master/vignettes/figures/fig1_balt_self_containment.png) for Hawaii

```{r}
# Install missing packages if needed:
# install.packages(c("lehdr", "tidycensus", "tidyverse", "sf", "viridis"))

library(lehdr)
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(viridis)

# 1. Pull LODES Origin-Destination (OD) data for Hawaii
# This gets all primary job commutes (JT01) for all workers (S000)
hi_od <- grab_lodes(
  state = "hi",
  year = 2021,
  lodes_type = "od",
  job_type = "JT01", 
  segment = "S000"   
)

# 2. Extract Census Tracts (first 11 digits of the 15-digit FIPS)
hi_tract_flows <- hi_od %>%
  mutate(
    h_tract = substr(h_geocode, 1, 11),
    w_tract = substr(w_geocode, 1, 11)
  )

# 3. Calculate metrics per Residence Tract
# Total workforce living in tract vs. those who also work there
hi_commute_stats <- hi_tract_flows %>%
  group_by(h_tract) %>%
  summarize(
    total_resident_workers = sum(S000),
    stay_in_tract = sum(S000[h_tract == w_tract]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_stay = (stay_in_tract / total_resident_workers) * 100
  )

# 4. Get Spatial Boundaries from Census (Filtering to Honolulu County for detail)
# Note: You can remove the county filter to map the whole state
hi_geometry <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "B08301_001", # Total workers 16+ (Census baseline)
  state = "HI",
  county = "Honolulu",       # Filters to Oahu for high-resolution mapping
  year = 2021,
  geometry = TRUE
)

# 5. Join spatial data with commuting stats
map_data <- hi_geometry %>%
  left_join(hi_commute_stats, by = c("GEOID" = "h_tract")) %>%
  replace_na(list(pct_stay = 0, stay_in_tract = 0))

# 6. Generate the Map
ggplot(data = map_data) +
  # Fixed: Changed color to an 8-character hex code (#FFFFFFFF with 33 for ~20% alpha)
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_stay), color = "#FFFFFF33", size = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako", 
    name = "% of Workers",
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Self-Contained Commuters in Honolulu County",
    subtitle = "Percentage of resident workers who stay within their home census tract for work",
    caption = "Data: US Census Bureau LEHD LODES (2021)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

```

```{r}
# Install mapview if you don't have it:
# install.packages("mapview")

library(mapview)

# Configure mapview options to use a clean background
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE) 

# Generate the interactive map
mapview(
  map_data, 
  zcol = "pct_stay",                # The column to color the tracts by
  col.regions = viridis::mako(100), # Color palette matching our ggplot
  layer.name = "% of Workers Staying",
  label = paste0("Tract: ", map_data$GEOID, " | Stay: ", round(map_data$pct_stay, 1), "%")
)

```

Challenge 2: Recreate t[his figure](https://github.com/jamgreen/lehdr/blob/master/vignettes/figures/fig2_md_job_change.png) for a state of your choosing

```{r}
# Install missing packages if needed:
# install.packages(c("lehdr", "tidycensus", "tidyverse", "sf", "mapview", "viridis"))

library(lehdr)
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(leafpop)

# 1. Pull Workplace Area Characteristics (WAC) data for Kansas
# Fixed: We add `agg_geo = "county"` to let lehdr handle the grouping automatically.
wac_2011 <- grab_lodes(
  state = "ks", 
  year = 2011, 
  lodes_type = "wac", 
  job_type = "JT01", 
  segment = "S000",
  agg_geo = "county"
)

wac_2021 <- grab_lodes(
  state = "ks", 
  year = 2021, 
  lodes_type = "wac", 
  job_type = "JT01", 
  segment = "S000",
  agg_geo = "county"
)

# 2. Extract job metrics using the correct column name ('C000' represents total counts)
county_jobs_2011 <- wac_2011 %>%
  select(county_fips = w_county, jobs_2011 = C000)

county_jobs_2021 <- wac_2021 %>%
  select(county_fips = w_county, jobs_2021 = C000)

# 3. Combine years and calculate Net Job Growth metrics
growth_data <- county_jobs_2011 %>%
  inner_join(county_jobs_2021, by = "county_fips") %>%
  mutate(
    net_change = jobs_2021 - jobs_2011,
    pct_growth = round((net_change / jobs_2011) * 100, 1)
  )

# 4. Fetch Kansas County geometry
ks_counties <- get_acs(
  geography = "county",
  variables = "B01001_001", # Baseline total population
  state = "KS",
  year = 2021,
  geometry = TRUE
)

# 5. Merge the spatial boundaries with job metrics
map_data <- ks_counties %>%
  left_join(growth_data, by = c("GEOID" = "county_fips")) %>%
  select(NAME, GEOID, jobs_2011, jobs_2021, net_change, pct_growth, geometry)

# 6. Initialize mapview options for clean background
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE)

# 7. Render Interactive Map (using percent growth)
mapview(
  map_data,
  zcol = "pct_growth",                     # Metric to shade counties by
  col.regions = viridis::rocket(100),       # High-contrast color palette
  layer.name = "Job Growth % (2011-2021)",
  popup = popupTable(
    map_data, 
    zcol = c("NAME", "jobs_2011", "jobs_2021", "net_change", "pct_growth")
  )
)


```

```{r}
# Combine both layers on a single map canvas
mapview(
  map_data,
  zcol = "net_change",
  col.regions = viridis::mako(100),
  layer.name = "Net Job Change (Count)",
  popup = leafpop::popupTable(
    map_data, 
    zcol = c("NAME", "jobs_2011", "jobs_2021", "net_change", "pct_growth")
  )
) + 
  mapview(
    map_data,
    zcol = "pct_growth",
    col.regions = viridis::rocket(100),
    layer.name = "Job Growth %",
    popup = leafpop::popupTable(
      map_data, 
      zcol = c("NAME", "jobs_2011", "jobs_2021", "net_change", "pct_growth")
    )
  )

```
